title: Blood pressure
summary: Log readings, see averages and trends, and share a report with your doctor
description:
**Blood pressure** is a private log for the readings you take at home with your own cuff. It does not measure blood pressure itself.

**What it does**

- **Log a reading** in seconds: upper (systolic) and lower (diastolic) numbers, pulse, time, arm, position (sitting, standing, lying down), whether your monitor showed an irregular heartbeat, context such as "before medication" or "after coffee", and a note.
- **Categories for every reading**, using the band set you choose: the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology guideline (2017, kept in the 2025 update: normal, elevated, high stage 1, high stage 2, very high) or the European Society of Cardiology 2024 guideline (not elevated, elevated, high, very high). Readings below 90/60 are marked low. Each category has its own icon and colour, always shown with its name.
- **A clear warning for very high readings**, with what to do: rest, measure again, call your doctor, and when to call emergency services.
- **Your latest reading** in large type with its category, and how it compares with your 30-day average.
- **Averages** for the last 7 and 30 days, mornings and evenings separately, and how many readings were below the target you set with your doctor.
- **Trends**: daily averages of the upper and lower numbers for 30 days, on bands that show the categories of the guideline you chose and with your target as a line, weekly averages for 6 months, pulse, and readings by category.
- **Reminders**, morning and evening by default, at the times and on the days you choose. A reminder is skipped if you logged a reading in the last two hours, and the overview ticks off the days of this week you measured.
- **A report for your doctor** for 7, 30 or 90 days or a year: averages, morning and evening averages, highest and lowest values, and every reading. Share it as text through any app you pick, or save a CSV file for a spreadsheet.
- **Bring your readings along**: import the CSV file most blood-pressure apps and connected-monitor apps export: date and time in one or two columns, upper and lower numbers, pulse, and where present arm, position, irregular heartbeat, context tags and notes, with commas or semicolons and month-first or day-first dates. Readings you already have are left out, so a newer export from the same app adds only the new ones.
- **App lock**: your readings stay behind your fingerprint, face or screen lock (on from the start; you can turn it off in the app’s Permissions after unlocking).
- **How to measure** at home, step by step.
- **In English or Slovak**, following your phone's language.

**What it never does**

- No ads, no subscriptions, no paywalled features.
- No account and no sign-in.
- No internet access at all: the app cannot connect to the internet, and your readings leave your phone only when you share or save them.
- No analytics or tracking of any kind.

**Not medical advice**

This app is a log, not a medical device, and does not diagnose anything. Categories describe single readings; only your doctor can diagnose high or low blood pressure, from several readings. If a reading is very high and you have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, a change in vision or trouble speaking, call your local emergency number.

research.used_for: ESC 2024 office blood pressure categories: not elevated below 120/70, elevated 120-139 or 70-89, hypertension 140/90 or more
Confirmation of the ESC 2024 bands and that ESC 2024 no longer grades hypertension in stages

AHA/ACC categories (normal below 120/80; elevated 120-129 and below 80; stage 1 130-139 or 80-89; stage 2 140 or 90 and over; above 180 and/or 120 severe), and the symptoms that make a very high reading an emergency (seen through search summaries; the page refused automated reading)
The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline keeps the 2017 categories and renames hypertensive urgency to severe hypertension (above 180/120)
Low blood pressure threshold: a reading below 90/60 mmHg
Home monitoring protocol (two readings, morning and evening, for 7 days): morning and evening averages, the default reminders and the how-to-measure steps
Home measurement preparation: seated rest, before medication, food or exercise; at least five to seven days of readings

What users expect from leaders: a doctor export with statistics, morning and evening averages and a chronological log with context tags; morning and evening reminders at chosen times (tags paywalled there)
Doctor report with overall, morning and evening averages and guideline category context
Pulse pressure and mean arterial pressure computed per reading; readings tagged with posture and arm; the app logs readings from a separate cuff
A connected-monitor export (blood_pressure.csv): header Date,"Heart rate",Systolic,Diastolic,Comments, dates as "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", pulse-only rows without pressure (imported as skipped rows)
That vendor's data export is CSV, with heart rate, systolic, diastolic and comments for blood pressure
A diary app's CSV export holds date and time, systolic, diastolic, pulse, tags and note: tags are added to the note
A monitor-cloud export layout: DateTimeLocal (ISO local time), Systolic, Diastolic, Pulse plus unit columns, which the import reads or ignores
A fitness-watch export (Time,Reading,Heart Rate,Category,Notes with "130 Sys / 87 Dia" in one cell and the date on its own line): not importable yet
A phone health store export (systolic, diastolic, pulse with timestamps) whose CSV starts with a metadata line: not importable yet

migration.summary: Imports the CSV most blood-pressure apps export: date and time, systolic and diastolic in mmHg or kPa, pulse, arm, position, irregular heartbeat, tags and notes; readings you have are left out

samples.about: This app’s own export, every column
Connected-monitor export: one date-time column, heart rate, systolic, diastolic, comments; a pulse-only row is skipped
US-style export: month-first dates, 12-hour times, units in the column names, irregular heartbeat yes or no
European-style export: semicolons, day-first dates with dots, SYS and DIA, arm and position
Monitor-cloud style export: local ISO date-time, unit columns that are ignored
Diary-style export: one date and time column, tags read as the reading’s context
